reason: The text depicts a stark differential treatment that supports this characterization. The Levites (Hebrew leaders) are selected, commanded by Yahweh, and explicitly promised blessing ('He will give upon you today a blessing'). In contrast, the common people are killed en masse—approximately 3,000 men—without apparent compassion or lament. The text shows Yahweh's concern manifested through elevation and reward of the leadership class (the Sons of Levi), while the broader populace is subject to severe judgment without mitigation. The absence of any expression of regret, compassion, or mercy toward the slain people, combined with the explicit blessing reserved for leaders who execute this judgment, supports a reading where preferential care is given to leaders while the people are treated with severity.
